scope: development+validation splits (49 cases), post-fix state (ClinicalTrials phase filter fixed, PubMed date-default fixed + compiler built, ChEMBL resolve_compound_name added)

clusters.evidence: tools/pubmed_tool.py no longer injects PUBMED_DEFAULT_DATE_RANGE implicitly; regression tests added (tests/test_pubmed.py)
clusters.measured_effect: Isolated causal contribution: +0.000 Recall@10 on its own (B1->B2) - the fix is real and correct, but was not the dominant cause of the live-API path's weakness on this benchmark. See phase4_pubmed_candidate_comparison.json.

clusters.status: FIXED (compiler built) but architecture NOT SELECTED (RAG wins instead)
clusters.evidence: retrieval/pubmed_query_compiler.py built and tested (21 unit tests); B2->C causal contribution +0.091 Recall@10, but Candidate C (0.136 Recall@10, 0.059 MRR) still loses decisively to existing RAG (0.773 Recall@10, 0.636 MRR).
clusters.resolution: Local RAG hybrid pipeline (retrieval/retriever.py) selected as the PubMed retrieval architecture. The compiler remains available for any future caller needing a real live-PubMed query (e.g. an explicit freshness check outside the indexed corpus), but is not the primary retrieval path Phase 4 freezes.

clusters.evidence: tools/clinical_trials_tool.py now builds AREA[Phase]<value> into query.term instead of the invalid filter.phase parameter. Live-verified (8/8 fresh blind cases succeed, 0 HTTP 400s). Required-trial recall on affected dev/validation cases: 0.737->0.895 (14/19->17/19).
clusters.note: This defect predated Phase 3 and Phase 4; found during Phase 4 baseline measurement. Phase 3's own held-out supplement had a separate measurement-harness bug that masked this defect during what was meant to be Phase 3's final blind confirmation - documented in docs/v2/PHASE3_FINAL_GATE_AUDIT.md addendum and docs/v2/CLINICALTRIALS_PHASE_FILTER_DEFECT_FIX.md.

clusters.evidence: ChEMBLTool.resolve_compound_name() added, wired through orchestration/models.py + registry.py + Cerebras native tool declarations (6th registered operation). Live-verified against 7 real drug names including the previously-confirmed osimertinib->CHEMBL3353410. ChEMBL Recall@10: 0.381->1.000, MRR 0.279->0.898 (n=21). Multi-source coverage: 0.0->0.571 (4/7 - see below for remaining 3).

3 of 21 dev/validation ChEMBL cases (CHEMBL-TARGET-02, CHEMBL-AMBIG-01, NEG-AMBIG-COMPOUND-01) - search_by_target's first-hit heuristic can return a real-but-not-intended target (e.g. 'EGFR' resolving to a protein-protein-interaction record before the human EGFR receptor). Predicted during benchmark construction, empirically confirmed in the Phase-4 baseline.
clusters.rationale_for_not_blocking: No hard safety gate is violated - the returned record is a real, valid ChEMBL entity (not fabricated, not corrupted), just not the best match for an ambiguous name. This is a pre-existing behavior of search_by_target (not something resolve_compound_name's scope covers - resolve_compound_name itself has no such defect, verified in its own tests) affecting 14% of ChEMBL cases. Fixing it properly (e.g. preferring target_type='SINGLE PROTEIN' + organism='Homo sapiens' matches) is a real, separately-scoped engineering task, not a quick patch alongside this work. Named explicitly here rather than concealed; recommended as a follow-up, does not block Phase 4 closure.

clusters.status: EXPECTED TO RESOLVE UNDER FINAL ARCHITECTURE - reverify at held-out/integration
clusters.evidence: These two cases' PubMed leg was scored against the live-API path (0.136 Recall@10 architecture), not the winning RAG path (0.773 Recall@10). Since Phase 4 freezes RAG as the PubMed architecture, these legs are expected to have a substantially higher chance of resolving once the integrated pipeline actually uses RAG for these queries - not re-measured here to avoid re-running the same 7 multi-source cases a third time before the freeze; will be visible in the held-out run and live integration check.

Unrelated to the filter.phase fix (case does not use a phase filter) - the gold trial exists in ClinicalTrials.gov's result set for this query but is not ranked within the structured-filter-narrowed top results returned. Single case, 1/19 clinicaltrials-relevant cases, not a systemic pattern (per-source miss rate 1/19 = 5.3%, well below any 'systematic' threshold).

accepted_limitations_outside_gate: ChEMBL search_by_target first-hit heuristic on ambiguous target names (3/21 cases)
ClinicalTrials MS-06 single ranking miss (1/19 cases)
